thread:
Ashley: heads-up — saw a sustained tail-latency spike (p95 -> p99) for dedicated-gpu-pool-eu3 over the last 8m. correlates with proxy egress buffer filling and host CPU stealing.
Miguel: ugh. any noisy tenant IDs?
Ashley: a few tenants show high egress flows. sample: tenant: tenant-42, tenant-77. stack traces show a lot of `proxy-worker` syscalls blocked. attaching snippet:
Ashley: ```
PROXY_EGRESS_QUEUE=98% used
host_cpu_iowait=18%
net_tx_drop=0
/var/log/proxy/worker.log:
  2026-03-21T16:07:02Z [warn] kvcache write stalled
  2026-03-21T16:07:03Z [error] proxy-worker: egress throttle applied
```
Sam: infra-bot just fired this alert 1s ago? @infra-bot can you paste the full alert? :eyes:
infra-bot: ALERT: eu3-proxy-egress-high-queue (severity=page) — queue depth > 90% for 6m, host_cpu_iowait > 15%
Miguel: two axes: (1) noisy-tenant policing + temp carveout, (2) quick route shift to fallback pool. prefer minimal customer-visible changes.
Rachel: I can run a temp carveout for the tenant-42/77 traffic and pin them to soft-dedicated slice if we want immediate isolation. that buys us time to debug root cause.
Len: what's impact to latency if we re-route to fallback eu2-dedicated? we saw ~12ms extra median last month.
Sam: 12ms is acceptable for these tenants (not prod SLA-critical). we should do a controlled shift. can someone run the reroute play?
Ashley: before reroute, i'd like to try a soft throttle and bump NIC tx queue to see if it reduces head-of-line blocking. quick commands:
Ashley: ```sh
# increase tx queue length temporarily
for iface in $(ls /sys/class/net | grep -E 'eth|ens'); do sudo ethtool -G $iface tx 512 || true; done
# tighten egress policer for tenant flows (example)
iptables -t mangle -A PROXY_EGRESS -m comment --comment tenant-42 -j CLASSIFY --set-class 1:42
```
Miguel: ethtool change is cheap, but needs sudo on host — automation?
Sam: i can run the ethtool change via the host-run job. Rachel — if you can create the carveout, i'll kick the reroute and then rollback the policer. we'll monitor p99s.
Rachel: doing carveout now. ETA ~ 90s.
deploy-bot: deploy:router-policy-v2 started by Rachel at 2026-03-21T16:09:10Z — canary to eu3-dedicated-slice-9
Ashley: policer tweak applied (tenant-42/77 -> limited egress 25Mbps) and ethtool tx bumped on hosts in rack-7.
Miguel: any telemetry from the probe?
Ashley: p95 back to baseline, p99 reduced ~45%. queue depth dropped to 42%. cpu iowait -> 6%.
Len: nice. so two mitigations worked: tx queue + soft policer + carveout. we still need root cause — why these tenants spiked egress (model or exploitation?).
Sam: agree. next steps: (A) trace tenant request patterns and identify the client SDKs, (B) run network capture on one of the offending proxy pods for 2 minutes, (C) add a scheduled job to detect sustained egress delta across tenants.
Miguel: i'll own (C) and a runbook update. Rachel/Sam — can you handle (A)/(B)?
Rachel: i'll check logs and ask support to contact tenant-42. Sam — want me to store pcap in /tmp/pcaps and link to the incident thread?
Sam: yes. use s3://redwood-temp/pcaps/<thread_ts>/ and post URL here. include tcpdump filter: `port 443 and host <tenant-ip>`
infra-bot: NOTE: temporary carveout created: eu3-slice-temp-1712468000 (expires 2h).
Ashley: moving to monitoring watch. if p99 creeps back up we revert carveout and fall back to full redirect to eu2.
Miguel: long-term: consider per-tenant egress budgeting on dedicated pools + automatic soft-isolation when sustained crossing of thresholds. I'll sketch proposal tomorrow.
Len: also log cost impact for dedicated slices when we bump up tx/queues — might increase CPU cycles and a small infra cost. capture delta and tag to the incident.
Ashley: thanks all — will update after packet analysis. :thumbsup:
